items.title: My Chemical Romance Face Legal Action From Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Over Stage Costumes
items.summary:
Pro Silver Star Ltd., the company that owns the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brand, has gone to court over My Chemical Romance's Hollywood Bowl residency, seeking a temporary restraining order and an injunction to stop the band from putting performers onstage in the squad's uniform. The filing targets a staging of "Teenagers" that the band reworked for the Los Angeles run, which opened Wednesday.

According to the legal documents, dancers dressed in Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders outfits appeared during the song, picked up rifles for a staged firefight, and were then shown being shot. Pro Silver Star says it asked the band to stop using the uniform before filing anything, and that My Chemical Romance declined.

The company's central complaint is confusion rather than content. "Audience members and online commentators understandably believed that the performers were the real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and said so in social media posts that continue to circulate," Pro Silver Star wrote in its filing.

The company went out of its way to say it is not objecting to the music or the message. "Silver Star is not litigious, and it takes no issue with MCR's music, its artistic ambitions, or any message Defendants seek to convey," the filing reads, adding that it is not asking the band to change its setlist, narrative, politics or choreography, or to remove the gun-toting performers — only to dress them in something else. "The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited," it argues.

Rolling Stone reported on the filing, noting that the band has not altered the bit in response. The Hollywood Bowl residency continued Friday night, and video from that show captured the cheerleaders back onstage in the same costumes.

items.title: Quentin Tarantino Wraps His AFI Fest Q&A By Showing Crowd First 17 Minutes Of ‘Cliff Booth’
items.summary:
Quentin Tarantino ended a Friday night Q&A at AFI Fest in Los Angeles by showing the audience the first 17 minutes of "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth," the sequel he wrote and David Fincher directed. The screening at the TCL Chinese Theatre followed a showing of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," and marked the first time any of the new film had been shown publicly.

Deadline reported that Tarantino was asked about the sequel near the end of the conversation and responded by offering the crowd a choice. "Well, I could talk a little bit about The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, or I could show you the first 17 minutes," he said, then stood up as the audience worked out what was happening.

Brad Pitt returns as Cliff Booth, the stuntman role that won him an Oscar in the 2019 original opposite Leonardo DiCaprio's Rick Dalton. The sequel jumps forward to 1977, with Booth working as a bartender and projectionist while fixing problems for Hollywood's powerful using what the logline calls his "unique (occasionally extralegal) abilities." The cast also includes Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis and Karren Karagulian.

Netflix has set a theatrical release for November 25 in Imax, with the film reaching the streaming service on December 23. Fincher told Empire earlier this week that Tarantino's first draft ran 230 pages and that he cut 60 of them. "It was essentially two movies," Fincher said. The finished cut runs roughly two and a half hours.

Tarantino also used the AFI Fest appearance to discuss "The Popinjay Cavalier," his first stage play, which will star Sacha Baron Cohen in London's West End. Previews begin February 23 at the Phoenix Theatre, with opening night set for March 18.

items.title: ‘Clayface’ Takes Shape As No. 1 With $24M+; ‘You Can See Everything’ Wowing With Possible $20M Second Weekend – Box Office Update
items.summary:
Warner Bros.' "Clayface" opened at No. 1 this weekend, pulling $10.4 million on Friday including previews and tracking toward a $24 million to $25 million three-day debut across 3,458 theaters. The James Watkins-directed DC film gives the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. operation a second consecutive weekend win.

Audiences gave "Clayface" an A- CinemaScore, matching James Gunn's "Superman" and well ahead of recent DC entries like "Supergirl" (B-) and "The Flash" (B). Moviegoers aged 18-34 made up 73% of the turnout, and the South and South Central regions overperformed. The film booked no Imax screens — "Street Fighter" holds those for two weeks — yet premium large formats still accounted for close to half the gross, with AMC Burbank leading at $51,000.

A24's "You Can See Everything" is the weekend's other story. The three-hour documentary co-directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder expanded by 1,800 theaters and posted a $6.1 million Friday, up 11% from its opening day, putting it on course for a $19 million to $20 million second weekend and a running total near $45 million. Deadline reported that some in the industry now see $80 million as a plausible domestic finish.

Laika's sixth feature, "Wildwood," opened to $4.2 million Friday and is heading for roughly $11 million through Fathom Entertainment across 2,942 theaters. The Travis Knight-directed film earned an A CinemaScore, matching "Kubo and the Two Strings," and is skewing toward adults — general audiences made up 94% of attendance, with parents and kids under 12 at just 7%.

Elsewhere, Black Bear's period sex comedy "Wicker," starring Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Elizabeth Debicki and Peter Dinklage, took $2.36 million Friday at 1,471 locations for a likely $5.5 million to $6 million start, with women making up 79% of the audience. "Street Fighter" fell 74% in its second weekend to $8.15 million, a steeper drop than "Mortal Kombat 2" managed in May. Sony's Taika Waititi-directed "Klara and the Sun," starring Jenna Ortega, managed $300,000 Friday at 880 locations for a $725,000 opening.

The full weekend is projected at $97.6 million, running 29% ahead of the same frame last year. Next weekend's outlook is less encouraging, with Halloween falling on a Saturday.
